id_and_class.theory_title: Nyāya’s Contingent Consciousness of the Enduring Self
id_and_class.summary: Nyāya holds that each person is an eternal, all-pervading, nonphysical self (ātman) that is not conscious by nature. Cognition, pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, and volition are contingent qualities that arise in the self only when it is linked through the inner organ (manas) to the senses, body, and objects. A cognition reveals its object but not itself; knowing that one knows takes a second, later inner perception.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as a Passing Quality of a Non-Conscious Self

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a set of adventitious qualities (āgantuka guṇa), chiefly awareness (jñāna) and felt affect, that inhere in a nonphysical self without being its essence.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mental qualities need a substrate, and no configuration of earth, water, fire, or air can bear them, so Nyāya infers a nonphysical self. The body, senses, and manas are causal conditions for experience, not its bearer.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Conditional arising (awareness is generated in the nonphysical self when self, manas, sense, and object come into contact; it does not emerge from matter and ceases when the conditions are removed)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Cognitions are object-directed: they present their objects through a relation of objecthood (viṣayatā). Subjectivity belongs to the self as owner of its qualities, yet the self is not conscious in itself, and awareness of one’s own awareness requires a separate apperception (anuvyavasāya).
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Colors, sounds, tastes, and smells are mind-independent qualities of external substances, so there is no puzzle of how a body produces redness. The inner qualitative states are the self’s own pleasure and pain, which makes felt valence the core of the mental.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Innumerable eternal, all-pervading, nonphysical selves; an atomic, permanent manas; sense faculties; mind-independent substances with real qualities; universals; memory traces (saṃskāra); and, in later Nyāya, a creator God.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through the knowledge-sources (pramāṇa) of perception, inference, comparison, and testimony. The self is inferred from its marks, and one’s own cognitions are known by inner perception through manas.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A chain from object to sense faculty, sense faculty to manas, and manas to self. Conscious life is a succession of intentional cognitions, affective states, and motivational states borne by one subject.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (affective); Perception; Introspection (higher-order); Memory; Attention; Personal identity
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Consciousness as a quality produced by contact among self, manas, sense, and object, combined with an extrinsic higher-order account of introspection.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Awareness is episodic. It lapses in dreamless sleep while the self persists, and in liberation all the self’s specific qualities, consciousness included, cease for good.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: The self is all-pervading, but experience occurs only where it is linked to a body through manas.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Cognitions, desires, and efforts move the self as agent, knower, and enjoyer. Manas carries memory traces between an experience and its recollection and, being permanent, across lives.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: An atomic manas links the self to one sensory stream at a time, which explains why experience is serial and selective. Nyāya argues from cross-modal and remembered integration (I touch what I saw) to a single enduring subject.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Perception is direct: cognition presents the external object’s real qualities rather than an inner replica. Introspection takes a prior cognition as its object through manas.
core_claims_and_evidence: Mental qualities require a substrate, and no material element can bear them, so the self is a nonphysical substance.
The self is not conscious in itself and persists without consciousness in dreamless sleep and liberation.
We do not experience through all five senses at once, so manas must be atomic and work one stream at a time.
A cognition does not reveal itself; awareness of it is a further inner perception, possible for any cognition but required for none, which blocks a regress.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical: inference by elimination, phenomenological observation, and centuries of interschool debate.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Dignāga and Dharmakīrti held that cognition is reflexively self-aware and charged that Nyāya’s view either regresses or leaves the first cognition unknown and unrememberable. Śaṅkara held awareness self-luminous and identical with the self. Advaita critics said a liberated Nyāya self is no different from a stone, and Bhāsarvajña dissented within Nyāya by allowing liberated bliss; Chadha questions whether the arguments establish a substantial self or only a minimal one.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Nyāya gives no account of why contact among self, manas, sense, and object should yield anything felt. An all-pervading, non-conscious self sits awkwardly with the local, perspectival character of experience.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Internally consistent: if awareness is a quality arising under conditions, removing the conditions removes it, and mainstream Nyāya accepts that consequence for liberation. Its position, substance dualism without essential consciousness, is rare.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since consciousness can only inhere in a nonphysical self, a material artifact cannot bear it.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: The self is eternal and manas carries memory traces across lives, so the subject survives death; in final liberation the self survives but consciousness ceases.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Nyāya’s psychology serves a path to liberation, the absolute cessation of suffering and rebirth.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Experience belongs to a nonphysical self, so copying bodily or neural patterns would not continue the person.
